chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

A group of people worshipped Allah out of desire for reward, so that is the worship of traders; and a group worshipped Allah out of fear, so that is the worship of slaves; and a group worshipped Allah out of gratitude, so that is the worship of free men.
ai.seo_question: What are the three levels of worship in Shia Islam based on intention?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) categorizes three levels of worship based on the underlying motive: worship driven by desire for reward is likened to traders, worship driven by fear of punishment is likened to slaves, and the highest form, worship driven by sincere gratitude to God, is the worship of free men. This tripartite classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of elevating 'shukr' (gratitude) as the essence of true servitude, distinguishing it from transactional or fear-based piety. The metaphor of 'free men' (al-ahrar) implies that those who worship out of pure thanksgiving are liberated from the bondage of self-interest and divine retribution.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 237. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

A group of people worshipped Allāh out of desire for reward surely, this is the worship of traders. Another group worshipped Allāh out of fear, this is the worship of slaves. Still another group worshipped Allāh out of gratefulness, this is the worship of free men.
